text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand what is going on, can you tell me more about the feeding difficulties and abdominal distension? Specifically, is the baby having trouble swallowing, or does he seem in pain during feeds?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby pass stool regularly, and has there been any blood or mucus noted in the diapers? I also need to know if there has been any vomiting, particularly if it is bilious or projectile.

text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any meconium within the first 48 hours of life, and have you observed any explosive watery stools after digital rectal examination? I need to rule out Hirschsprung disease given the history of delayed stooling and abdominal distension. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

text: Since the biopsy is normal, Hirschsprung is unlikely, so I need to check for other causes of obstruction. Does the baby have a history of eczema or other allergic reactions, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in the stools recently? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal biopsy and ultrasound, I suspect Intussusception might be masked or atypical, so I need to rule out mechanical obstruction. Has the baby passed any stool at all since the symptoms began, and can you describe the consistency of any recent stools? REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema
